survivingClaim: Precise obstruction; no statement about zeros of zeta. For the Fejer-tapered section of the prime chain on the gamma one-port, L_F(s) = sum_rho K_u(s - rho) on Re s > 0 with Re K_u >= 0 on Re w >= 0; hence the section is J-contractive on Re s > 1/2 + eta_0 for every P if zeta has no zero there, and a uniform lower bound along any sequence P_j -> infinity on that half-plane excludes zeros there (Harnack, Vitali). This is a Fejer-smoothed form of the known criterion Re xi'/xi > 0 and of map row P45, so the stage inequality at unbounded P is the target itself. With P = t^theta the statement follows from RH, is proved unconditionally only for P up to about ((1/4) log t log log t)^2 (where it also holds for every sign twist), and its band-bound consequence (Proposition 4, valid for arbitrary coefficients, constant not explicit) is also met by random sign chains. Sharp sections of zeta are J-expansive on the line for theta >= 1/2 (measured). Measured (float64, heights where RH is verified): zeta min Re L_F > 0 in all cells including an independent cell at t = 3000; sign chains, Liouville, DH and random unimodular twists violate for theta >= 1; DH's violation is the term of its off-line pair. No step uses multiplicativity; controls fail only through zero location or the absence of the identity. Class U7 closes as a row; R1 to R4 all false.

With P = t^theta the statement follows from RH and is proved only for P up to about ((1/4) log t log log t)^2, where it also holds for every sign twist; its band-bound consequence (Proposition 4) is met by random sign chains. Sharp sections of zeta are J-expansive on the line for theta >= 1/2 (MEASURED). No step uses multiplicativity; controls fail only through zero location. Proposition 5 (theta-coupled statement forces beta - 1/2 <= c_theta/log gamma) is neither proved nor refuted.

lesson: A tapered section makes the limit step sound (the positive-real class is closed and Harnack gives compactness), which moves the whole target into the stage inequality at unbounded P. Tying P to t^theta only weakens the target to (argued) a neighbourhood of the line of width c/(theta log t). Band-by-band square-root bounds do not separate zeta from random sign chains; the one-sided sum over all bands does, and that is the Weil form.
